newsitem.title: UK: RMC drops after cautious results statement.
newsitem.headline: RMC drops after cautious results statement.

text.p: Shares in building materials group RMC Plc dropped in early trading on Thursday after the company posted first-half results in line with expectations but warned of continued weak demand particularly in Germany.
The stock was down 27-1/2p at 11.25 stg by 0705 GMT.

"It is looking a bit bleak," said analyst Robin Hardy at Panmure Gordon. "The decline in Germany is quite severe and the company's statement gives no great hope that things will be better in the second half."
He said full-year estimates would probably be lowered on the back of the results.

Arend Dikkers, an analyst at Salomon Brothers, said the results were in line with his expectations but he would trim his full-year pre-tax profit forecast of 323 million stg on the back of the first-half statement.
Dikkers said RMC was particularly exposed in Germany to the weak commercial and public infrastructure sectors where demand was most under pressure.
In its statement, RMC said pre-tax profit dropped to 95.8 million stg from 130.3 million a year before, compared with analysts' expectations in a range between 90.0 million stg and 111.0 million.
It raised its dividend to 7.8p per share from 7.45p, compared with expectations between 7.7p and 8.2p.

The company said severe weather in the first quarter of the year had hit construction activity, particularly in Germany, and that in the UK hopes for an upturn in house building had failed to materialise.
Prospects for the second half were mixed, RMC said, and full-year results were not expected to reach the record levels of 1995.

Andrew Melrose, analyst at Paribas Capital Markets, said the statement added weight to his view that demand in Germany would remain weak for some time to come, as the government squeezes spending to meet targets for European monetary union.
"I would highlight that they are making clear that demand in Germany will experience a further fall," Melrose said, "and that allies with my feeling that this is not a temporary hiccup."

"I think Germany will remain tough for the next three years and I don't think the degree of recovery in the UK, France and Spain over that timeframe will be sufficient to generate much earnings momentum."
"Earnings prospects remain flat and I would retain my sell recommendation," Melrose said.
Shares in Redland Plc, also heavily exposed to the German market, were marked down 7p at 458 by 0729 GMT.
